Vanessa —

Quick intro: I’m Michael Norton (Cloud & AI platform lead at TechNexus). We’ve run CloudRidge for the last 18 months but our renewal is coming up and your team was recommended by a partner. Before we invest time on a demo, can you provide a concise comparison of the economics to replace CloudRidge?

Key asks:
- High-level per-token / per-embedding unit economics for comparable throughput (90th pct latency targets)
- Any migration credits or term concessions you can offer for an on-prem + hosted hybrid deployment
- Typical procurement timeline (SOW / PO / invoicing cadence)

We have a competing firm’s anchor already: 18% off list + $40k migration credits for a 12-month commit. Can Redwood match or beat that?

If helpful, I can share their quote. Susan (cc) is our procurement lead.

Thanks,
Michael
Michael Norton

TechNexus

Michael —

Appreciate the context. I pulled together a short competitive playbook and a baseline pricing model so you and Susan can see apples-to-apples numbers quickly. High level: Redwood can align to parity on list pricing and compete on total cost of ownership via our KV-caching, prefix caching, and a tailored batching profile — that typically reduces token spend 12–20% vs a straight replacement.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Baseline parity: match base list per-token and per-embed rates for equivalent model families
- Concessions: we can offer a targeted concession (discount or one-time migration credit) per the procurement ask — see options below
- Terming: 12-month minimum for committed discounts; 24-month for deeper discounts + reserved capacity

Suggested initial offers (you can pick one):
1) 10% off list for 12-month committed spend, plus $30k migration credit (applied as invoice credit over first 3 months)
2) 14% off list for 24-month committed reserved capacity (guaranteed throughput) + $20k migration credit
3) No up-front discount but $45k migration & integration credit for a 6-month pilot that converts to committed pricing after pilot acceptance

I attached: competitive_playbook_v1.pdf (playbook + talking points) and replacement_pricing_model.xlsx (line-item TCO).

Next steps: if any of these align, we can have Connor run a one-page concession approval and Evelyn can draft the procurement checklist and DocuSign package.

Would a quick 30-min alignment call with procurement on Wed work?

Best,

Michael / Vanessa —

I ran the numbers on the attached pricing model and isolation scenarios. Short version: given TechNexus's projected monthly token volume (provided during intro call), a 10% list discount + $30k migration credit yields net effective savings of ~11% in month 1 and ramps to ~15% over months 2–6 due to caching improvements and reduced inference cache misses. The 14% / 24-month reserved route yields better long-term unit economics but requires forecasted commitment.

Operational note: the migration credit assumes Redwood provides a migration engineer bundle (up to 80 hours) and an onboarding SLA. If procurement needs a stronger SLA (4 hr response, dedicated TAM), that increases credit usage.

If the competitor is at 18% + $40k credit, we can match the economics by either: (A) 12% discount + $40k credit for 12 months (one-time approval request), or (B) keep the 10% list discount and add a $50k migration & integration credit if they sign within 30 days. Option B is my recommended path because it preserves list parity and gives TechNexus more migration runway.

I'll prepare a one-page concession memo for approvals if Vanessa gives greenlight.

Connor O'Brien
Senior Deals Ops | Redwood Inference
